q1_issues.issue: the closing value "at $6.83" is unencoded — no `MeasureTo` on the eventuality and no `Measure` on the shares, so the sentence's principal figure is absent from the parse.
the delta "up 2 cents" is unencoded — the instruction set's scalar-change "was up / down" state carries exactly this as `(MeasureBy … 2 cent)`, and a stated qualifier is never silently dropped.

q2_gaps: a verbless absolute adjunct "…, up 2 cents": the scalar-change section gives the copular "was up / down" state but no reduced/appositive form, so which eventuality the delta attaches to is unsettled

"ended at <price>" as a closing-value predicate: *end* is not among the listed change-of-value verbs (rise/fall/climb/drop/gain/lose/ease/jump/slip), so whether the clause is a scalar change (subject `Theme`, figure `MeasureTo`) or an ordinary intransitive is undetermined
notes: What is emitted is correct — bare-plural episodic subject as a group witness, `(Weekday wednesday)` time term, `Past` — but the parse records only "shares ended Wednesday" and loses both numbers. If "ended at" is read as the scalar change that "up 2 cents" implies, the subject would also be `Theme` rather than `Patient` (statement 2).
